data.ruling: The datasheet verifier's refutation stands. The part fails 'D+/D- steady voltage (V12)'. V12 is the owner's answer to the question "What highest voltage may the USB protection let reach USB_DP and USB_DM (QFN-80 pins 67 and 66)?" and sets the highest steady voltage those pins may see: 3.63 V (owner, 2026-09-28). The TPD6E05U06 is a unidirectional shunt TVS (transient voltage suppressor) clamp to GND. It has a reverse stand-off of 5.5 V at IIO < 10 uA and a breakdown of 6.5 V min to 8.5 V max at 1 mA. SLVSBO7O section 6.4 states that it "triggers when voltages are above VBR" and is passive below that. It therefore lets any steady voltage from 3.63 V up to at least 5.5 V, and up to 6.5 V at worst, reach USB_DP and USB_DM through the 27 Ohm series resistor. D+ or D- shorted to the 5 V VBUS of the shared USB-C connector (V10, V13) is such a fault. P2 marked the check as passing on the ground that a shunt clamp "adds no source". That reading passes every passive part and leaves the owner's steady limit with no effect. P2's own record states that the part "does not limit a steady external voltage between 3.63 V and its breakdown". The USB 2.0 5V Short Circuit Withstand ECN (Engineering Change Notice) removes the short-to-VBUS withstand requirement from the transceiver and leaves it to "an external hub or other external protection circuitry". Meeting 3.63 V therefore needs a series or overvoltage-limiting element, which this part does not have. The stock verifier confirmed the part, and its figures show no fault in lifecycle, allowlist or LCSC identity: TI ACTIVE, Digi-Key Active, LCSC C962978 is TPD6E05U06RVZR in USON-14. The failure is this function's V12 requirement against a shunt-clamp part, so the scope is function. The part itself does not fail.
data.evidence:
SLVSBO7O (December 2012, revised August 2024), 2801466 bytes, SHA-256 c167cf1e72a5473a4d2c59b6a3c0251498701da05b7785919b9ceaae3b3e02c6, the same file the verifier read.
- Recommended Operating Conditions: VIO 0 to 5.5 V.
- Section 5.4: VRWM 5.5 V max at IIO < 10 uA. VBR 6.5 V min, 8.5 V max at IIO = 1 mA. VClamp 10 V at 1 A and 14 V at 5 A TLP (transmission-line pulse), typical.
- Section 6.3.5: "The DC breakdown voltage of each I/O pin is a minimum of 6.5V ... surges above the reverse standoff voltage of 5.5V."
- Section 6.4: "a passive integrated circuit that triggers when voltages are above VBR or below the lower diodes Vf (-0.6 V)".
- Research.md:572 (V12) at commit 10b0bade34de: "Steady: 3.63 V. ESD: clamping voltage at most 36 V at 16 A TLP ... ahead of the 27 Ω series resistor (owner, 2026-09-28)".
- Research.md V10 and V13: one USB-C connector shared with the F8 charger input, VBUS 5.5 V at 3 A.
- P2's FU return (scratch/FU-A1/P2-R1/return.json) reports under 'USB_DP and USB_DM steady overvoltage' that no shortlisted part limits a steady external voltage on D+ or D- to 3.63 V.
- USB 2.0 '5V Short Circuit Withstand ECN.pdf', lines 69-70: "OEMs that require short circuit withstand to VBUS can implement the requirement with an external hub or other external protection circuitry."
- Every other figure the two verifiers checked passes as they reported. The only failed check is 'D+/D- steady voltage (V12)'.
